proof_scope: regression cases for defects observed in live operation, run against the real CLI and the real routing library with an isolated state root, including landed repair-worktree cleanup through ops-worktrees

claims.proves: each named failure mode is refused or handled as described, repeatably, through the skill's own entrypoint and routing functions; that the installed cron interval is never every-minute, that dispatch defers during the overnight batch window, that activate reports schedule and state together, and that auto-landed repairs invoke ops-worktrees cleanup before issue closure
claims.does_not_prove: that a live repair, closure audit, or completion attestation succeeds. Those dispatch models through $ask/Tau and are proven only by a live receipt read back from the produced artifact, not by this fixture.

cases.name: project-watchdog-ui-snapshot-contract
command: ../run.sh ui-data --receipt-limit 2 | jq -e '.schema == "agent_skills.project_watchdog.ui_snapshot.v1" and (.items | type == "array") and (.counts | has("TOTAL"))' >/dev/null && node ../ui/scripts/check-ui-contract.mjs
cases.proves: The project-watchdog UI data projection emits the declared read-only snapshot schema and the React/Tailwind interface keeps data-qid/data-qs-action/title, useRegisterAction, sticky filters, desktop table, mobile cards, Tau DAG, and receipt-chain contract literals.
cases.does_not_prove: A human has opened the UI in a browser or that a live Tau run is embedded; those require a local browser interaction receipt after serving the built app.

cases.name: closure-audit-nonzero-needs-attention
cases.proves: A closure audit whose Ask/Tau wrapper exits nonzero but whose seats declare VERDICT: NEEDS_ATTENTION is not sent down the no-verdict path; it attempts durable closure-unverified handling and records cooldown state so the next tick does not re-launch the duplicate audit.
cases.does_not_prove: A live browser/provider closure audit succeeds; this is a fault-injected regression over the watchdog's own handler and cooldown path.

cases.name: closure-audit-nonzero-fail-reopens
cases.proves: A closure audit whose Ask/Tau wrapper exits nonzero because receipt evidence records VERDICT: FAIL still reaches the FAIL/reopen path instead of being downgraded to no usable panel verdict and retried forever.
cases.does_not_prove: A live browser/provider closure audit succeeds; this is a fault-injected regression over the watchdog handler path observed from issue #1519 receipts.

cases.name: closure-auditors-use-local-claude-not-webclaude
cases.proves: The default project-watchdog closure-audit roster uses the local Ask/Tau Claude Opus low-reasoning lane instead of the webclaude browser test seat, and markdown receipt paths from issue comments are read relative to the target project worktree.
cases.does_not_prove: A live closure audit provider call succeeds; this is a deterministic configuration guard.

cases.name: dirty-registered-target-does-not-block-isolated-authoring
cases.proves: A dirty target path in the registered checkout is reported but does not block project-watchdog from preparing an isolated repair worktree from origin/main.
cases.does_not_prove: A live Ask/Tau repair for the ticket succeeds.

cases.name: skill-scoped-projects-only-route-owned-targets
cases.notes: Regression for Battle scope drift: a battle-scoped project sees only skills/battle issues, and the broad agent-skills project can exclude skills/battle so fleet rotation does not steal Battle tickets.

cases.name: auto-landed-repair-worktree-cleanup
cases.proves: After a reviewer-passed repair lands on main, project-watchdog invokes ops-worktrees archive --apply for the repair worktree before closing; if cleanup fails, the ticket stays open and is marked needs-attention.
cases.does_not_prove: A live GitHub repair branch was landed or a real filesystem worktree was archived; these tests mock the GitHub and subprocess effects and prove watchdog control flow only.

cases.name: agent-actionable-attention-is-not-human-blocker
cases.proves: A completion-attestation transport/parser failure remains unproven but is marked requires_human_input=false with authorized_agent_next_steps, and the top-level tick can complete without training supervising agents to stop for a fake human blocker.
cases.does_not_prove: A live completion attestation succeeds; this is a deterministic regression over watchdog control flow and handler metadata.

cases.name: overlapping-applied-ticks-skip-live
command:
cd ..; D=$(mktemp -d); printf '%s
' '{"schema":"agent_skills.project_watchdog.registry.v1","projects":[]}' > $D/projects.json; printf '%s
' '{"global":{"state":"active"},"projects":{}}' > $D/state.json; PROJECT_WATCHDOG_STATE_ROOT=$D PROJECT_WATCHDOG_PROJECTS_PATH=$D/projects.json PROJECT_WATCHDOG_TEST_HOLD_LOCK_SECONDS=8 ./run.sh tick --apply --project all --max-tickets 1 > $D/first.out 2> $D/first.err & first=$!; for i in $(seq 1 80); do [ -f $D/lock/owner.json ] && break; sleep 0.1; done; test -f $D/lock/owner.json || { echo FIRST_LOCK_NOT_OBSERVED; cat $D/first.err; kill $first 2>/dev/null || true; wait $first 2>/dev/null || true; exit 1; }; python3 - <<PY
import json, pathlib
p=pathlib.Path('$D/lock/owner.json')
d=json.loads(p.read_text())
d['epoch']=0
p.write_text(json.dumps(d, indent=2)+'\n')

PY
PROJECT_WATCHDOG_STATE_ROOT=$D PROJECT_WATCHDOG_PROJECTS_PATH=$D/projects.json ./run.sh tick --apply --project all --max-tickets 1 > $D/second.out 2> $D/second.err; second_rc=$?; wait $first; first_rc=$?; python3 - <<PY
import json, pathlib, sys
root=pathlib.Path('$D')
second_rc=int('$second_rc')
first_rc=int('$first_rc')
second=json.loads((root/'second.out').read_text())

assert second['status']=='SKIPPED', second
assert second['stop_reason']=='tick_already_running', second
assert second.get('handled_issues') == [], second.get('handled_issues')
assert second.get('receipt_persisted') is False, second
assert first_rc == 0, (first_rc, (root/'first.err').read_text())
print('OVERLAP_SKIPPED_LIVE')
PY
